draft.change: Add חִוִּי as a gentilic noun under its own consonants, חוי. The genealogy establishes its ethnic sense and gives no verbal derivation.
draft.definition: A member of the Hivite people, or the Hivites collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:17 lists the Hivites among Canaan’s descendants. Genesis 34:2 uses the same gentilic of an individual, Hamor.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 10:17, וְאֶת introduces הַחִוִּי just as it introduces the Arkites and the Sinites. All three continue the list of Canaan’s descendants begun in verse 15. Verse 18 calls them Canaanite clans.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute gentilic noun. The singular designates the people collectively.

draft.change: Add Genesis 10:17 as evidence for definite-object in word 0 of article 2t.
draft.definition: Introduces the particular person or thing a verb acts on, ordinarily a definite noun identified by the article, a name or a possessive suffix.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 10:17, וְאֶת הַעַרְקִי adds the Arkite to the objects of יָלַד in Genesis 10:15.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 10:15 Canaan is the subject of יָלַד, “fathered.” The list of his descendants continues in verse 17, where the marked וְאֶת introduces הַעַרְקִי, “the Arkite,” between the Hivite and the Sinite. Each takes its own object marker.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins the next item in the list. The unsuffixed direct-object particle אֶת introduces הַעַרְקִי.
analysis.sense: Marks the Arkite as a definite direct object of יָלַד.

draft.change: Add the Hebrew gentilic עַרְקִי with its collective sense and correct the occurrence gloss from “Naphtali” to “the Arkites.”
draft.definition: An Arkite, a member of one of the Canaanite clans. The definite singular designates the clan collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:17 names the Arkites between the Hivites and Sinites. The parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 1:15 preserves the same sequence.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 10:17, וְאֶת marks the Arkites as an object alongside the Hivites and Sinites in the genealogy of Canaan. Genesis 10:18 calls the groups in this list Canaanite clans.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular gentilic noun in the absolute state. The ending ־ִי marks affiliation. The singular denotes the people collectively.

draft.change: Add סִינִי as a gentilic noun under nouns/. The reported data/lexicon/syny.json is absent from the checkout. The form supplies the consonantal base סינ, and the genealogy gives no evidence for deriving it from סחר.
draft.definition: A member of the Sinite clan. The definite singular can designate the Sinites collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:17 lists the Sinites after the Hivites and Arkites. First Chronicles 1:15 repeats the same sequence.

analysis.evidence: The repeated וְאֶת places הַסִּינִי alongside הַחִוִּי and הַעַרְקִי as the third people named in Genesis 10:17. Verse 18 calls the groups in this list Canaanite clans.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial ס of סִינִי. The noun has the gentilic ending ־ִי and is masculine singular absolute. Here the singular designates the whole clan.
analysis.sense: A member of the Sinite clan among Canaan’s descendants, used collectively here for the clan.
